chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ali ibn al-Fad al-Fadl al-Wasiti, who said:
I wrote to him: 'When the sun or the moon is eclipsed and I am riding and am not able to dismount,' he wrote to me: 'Pray upon your mount upon which you are.'
ai.seo_question: How to perform eclipse prayer while riding?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the principle of ease (yusr) in Shia jurisprudence, demonstrating that the Imam’s directive to pray while riding is a specific concession for those physically unable to dismount, rather than a general permission to neglect standing. It underscores the flexibility of ritual posture (qiyam) in eclipse prayers, aligning with the broader Shia emphasis on removing hardship during acts of worship. The ruling reflects the practical application of divine mercy, ensuring that the obligation of Salat al-Kusuf remains accessible even in transient or constrained circumstances.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Imran Bin Musa, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Ali Bin Al-Fazl Al-Wasity who said,
‘I wrote to himasws, ‘When either the sun or the moon is eclipsed and I am riding, I am not able upon the dismounting’. So heasws wrote to me: ‘Pray Salāt upon your ride which you are upon’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Imran ibn Musa from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Majid from Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Wasitiy who has said the following:

“I once wrote to him (the Imam), Alayhi al-Salam, asking, ‘If a sun or moon eclipse takes place and I am riding and unable to dismount what must I do?’ He (the Imam) wrote to me, ‘Perform Salah (prayer) on your stumper which you ride.’”
